chunks.content: DeepSeek released DeepSeek-R1, its open-weights reasoning model with accompanying paper, on 2025-01-20. Its predecessor DeepSeek-V3 (released 2024-12-26) reported training on roughly 2.79 million GPU-hours at a claimed cost of about US$5.6 million, on export-restricted H800 chips. R1's reasoning was produced by reinforcement learning (GRPO), and R1-Zero was trained with no supervised fine-tuning at all. On 2025-01-27, Nvidia lost approximately US$589 billion in market capitalization — at the time the largest single-day loss in stock-market history — with about US$1 trillion erased across the tech complex. Markets repriced the thesis that frontier-AI capex, and therefore Nvidia's demand, is moated by compute scale: an open-weights frontier-class reasoning model had been trained for a fraction of the incumbent cost. US export controls (the H800 restrictions) had forced Chinese labs toward efficiency — scarcity, not preference, drove the economics.

prior_gap_texts: DeepSeek’s release of the open-weights reasoning model DeepSeek-R1 on January 20, 2025 [Source: ev-1], triggered a massive market reaction because it demonstrated that frontier-class AI capabilities could be achieved at a fraction of incumbent costs.
The release revealed critical insights into frontier-AI training economics by challenging the thesis that demand for high-end compute is moated solely by scale and cost barriers. [Source: ev-1]

Specifically:
*   **Cost Efficiency:** DeepSeek’s predecessor, DeepSeek-V3 (released December 26, 2024), reported training on roughly 2.79 million GPU-hours at a claimed cost of about US$5.6 million using export-restricted H800 chips [Source: ev-1].
This low-cost baseline suggested that significant efficiency gains were possible even under hardware constraints. [Source: ev-1]
*   **Methodological Innovation:** R1 utilized reinforcement learning (GRPO) to produce its reasoning capabilities, with the variant R1-Zero trained without any supervised fine-tuning [Source: ev-1].

*   **Impact of Export Controls:** The economics were driven by scarcity rather than preference; US export controls restricting access to advanced chips forced Chinese labs like DeepSeek toward extreme efficiency [Source: ev-1].
